zh.title: 波音完成13顆O3b mPOWER衛星星座部署
zh.summary: 波音完成O3b mPOWER星座部署；衛星預計2027年中投入服務
body: 波音（Boeing）宣布，O3b mPOWER衛星F11、F12與F13已完成發射並加入軌道上既有的10顆衛星，完成共13顆衛星的O3b mPOWER星座部署。此次發射在卡納維爾角太空軍基地（Cape Canaveral Space Force Station）進行，時間為2026年9月13日。
波音表示，此里程碑使合作夥伴SES得以顯著擴展高速連線服務，滿足持續成長的頻寬需求。使用O3b mPOWER網路服務的客戶包括郵輪、政府機構、民用實體、行動電信業者與商業航空公司。
O3b mPOWER F11、F12與F13在完成軌道抬升與初期作業後，預計於2027年中投入服務。波音表示，該星座採軟體定義酬載技術，可動態調整頻寬與波束功率。

en.title: Boeing completes 13-satellite O3b mPOWER constellation with final launch
en.summary: Boeing completes O3b mPOWER constellation; final satellites to enter service in mid-2027
body: Boeing announced that the final three O3b mPOWER satellites, F11, F12 and F13, have joined 10 already in orbit following a successful launch from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, completing the 13-satellite O3b mPOWER constellation. The announcement was made on September 13, 2026.

The company said the milestone enables partner company SES to significantly expand high-speed connectivity, with active customers including cruise lines, government organizations, civil entities, mobile operators and commercial airlines.

Boeing stated that O3b mPOWER F11, F12 and F13 are forecast to enter service in mid-2027 after completing orbit raising and initialization activities. The constellation uses software-defined payload technology to dynamically route bandwidth and adjust capacity in real time.

zh.title: 美國FAA要求達美與Breeze檢查13架A220燃油管
zh.summary: FAA針對13架A220發布燃油軟管檢查令；扭轉缺陷引發洩漏火險
body: 美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）發布指令，要求達美航空與Breeze Airways旗下共13架空中巴士A220客機檢查燃油軟管。該指令源於發現燃油軟管存在扭轉缺陷，引發燃油洩漏與潛在火災風險憂慮。
Simple Flying報導指出，FAA鎖定這13架美國註冊A220執行燃油軟管檢查，旨在消除扭轉缺陷導致的燃油洩漏與火險隱憂。兩家航空公司須依指令時程完成檢查作業，確保機隊燃油系統符合安全標準。

en.title: FAA Orders Breeze Airways and Delta Air Lines to Inspect 13 Airbus A220 Fuel Hose Lines
en.summary: FAA orders fuel hose inspections on 13 A220s operated by Breeze and Delta; twisting defect raises leak and fire concerns
body: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued an order requiring Breeze Airways and Delta Air Lines to inspect fuel hose lines on 13 Airbus A220 aircraft registered in the United States. The directive follows the discovery of a twisting defect in the fuel hoses that raised concerns over potential fuel leaks and fire risks.

According to Simple Flying, the FAA is targeting these 13 U.S.-registered A220s for fuel hose inspections to address the twisting defect. Both airlines must comply with the inspection schedule to ensure the fuel systems meet safety standards and eliminate the leak and fire hazards.
